topics.title: Anthropic proposes public-benefit share fund
topics.summary: AI company Anthropic says it plans to commit 5% of its shares to a public-benefit fund, with the proposal subject to shareholder approval.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a huge tech company had money set aside for the public good, what would you hope it funded first: libraries, parks, training, research, or something delightfully weird?

topics.title: China reports export-led growth
topics.summary: China reported 4.5% year-over-year third-quarter growth, with electronics and AI-related exports helping industry outpace consumer spending.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a new technology boom arrives, what changes first in everyday life: jobs, shopping, school, entertainment, or the gadgets cluttering the kitchen?

topics.title: UK pledges stronger support for disabled flyers
topics.summary: The UK government says planned aviation measures would strengthen help for disabled passengers, including protections for mobility aids and new enforcement powers.
topics.discussionPrompt: What small change would make travel feel dramatically easier for you: clearer signs, quieter waiting areas, better seating, friendly staff, or luggage that follows instructions?

topics.title: Seabirds rebound on England’s south coast
topics.summary: Conservation work has helped seabird colonies in the Solent recover after bird flu losses, with sandwich terns returning from zero to 756 breeding pairs.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could help one local animal thrive, which would you choose: birds, bees, frogs, fish, or the mysterious creature that raids the compost bin?

topics.title: Countries gather for the COP17 nature summit
topics.summary: Countries are meeting in Armenia to review progress on global biodiversity promises, with pressure mounting to turn conservation targets into practical action.
topics.discussionPrompt: Big nature goals can sound abstract. What is one change you could actually picture in your neighborhood that would make it feel more alive?

topics.title: Orionid meteors light up October skies
topics.summary: The Orionid meteor shower is arriving as Earth passes through debris from Halley’s comet, offering skywatchers a chance to spot fast streaks of light.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you stay up late for a meteor shower if the sky were clear, or do you prefer appreciating space from somewhere with snacks and central heating?

topics.title: Austrian growers revive heritage apples
topics.summary: An Austrian initiative is bringing neglected apple varieties back into orchards, pairing local food traditions with efforts to preserve agricultural diversity.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could bring back one forgotten food or flavor, what would make the cut: a family recipe, an old candy, a regional dish, or something from childhood?

topics.title: Venues set limits on influencer photoshoots
topics.summary: Some hotels, restaurants and beauty spots are restricting commercial-style social-media shoots as businesses try to balance visitors, staff and online promotion.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a café became famous online overnight, would you be excited by the buzz or miss being able to find a quiet table without a ring light nearby?

topics.title: The Simpsons gives Apu a new voice
topics.summary: The Simpsons has cast actor Sunil Malhotra as the new voice of Apu, a change presented as part of the show’s effort to revisit a long-running character.
topics.discussionPrompt: When an old TV show updates a familiar character, do you enjoy the fresh take, or does your brain insist that the original version lives forever?

topics.title: Australian musicians raise AI training concerns
topics.summary: Australia’s music sector says songs including Kylie Minogue tracks have already been used in AI training, renewing debate over consent and creative rights.
topics.discussionPrompt: If an AI learned from music you loved, what would feel fair: payment, permission, credit, an opt-out button, or a tiny robot concert ticket?
